headline: Five CRITICALs are live in the shipped product. Two are navigation dead ends - signed-in users cannot reach /guide, /terms or /privacy at all, and six CTAs on those very pages render a blank white screen. One is a measured WCAG failure (1.31:1 against a 4.5:1 floor). Two silently destroy user data: a nested settings write discards its siblings, and an idempotency key charge() accepts and never uses means a retried settlement bills twice. findings.title: Shallow merge in update_user_settings silently destroys nested keys

evidence.observed: MEASURED with deepcopy so aliasing cannot mask it: applying {'ai':{'detection':{'enabled':True}}} onto {'ai':{'detection':{'enabled':False,'min_human':70,'paid_verification':'off'}}} yields {'enabled':True}. LOST KEYS: ['min_human','paid_verification']. `current[k].update(v)` merges exactly one level, so a two-level write replaces its whole subtree.

findings.impact: A user who sets a detection threshold and later toggles detection loses the threshold, silently. The same defect is already documented on the CLIENT (SettingsApp.mergeSettings), so fixing one side alone leaves the data loss. It also makes any two-level scoped-override write destructive.

fix.approach: Deep-merge dicts recursively. `scoped` stays REPLACE_ON_WRITE (it is a document), so the recursion must respect that opt-out.

REPLACE_ON_WRITE = frozenset({"scoped"})


def _deep_merge(base: dict, patch: dict) -> dict:
    """Merge dicts recursively. Scalars and LISTS replace.

    Lists replace rather than append deliberately: these are configuration values
    (style samples, enabled detectors) and appending would make removal impossible -
    the same reason `scoped` is REPLACE_ON_WRITE.
    """
    out = dict(base or {})
    for k, v in (patch or {}).items():
        if isinstance(v, dict) and isinstance(out.get(k), dict):
            out[k] = _deep_merge(out[k], v)
        else:
            out[k] = copy.deepcopy(v)
    return out

findings.title: A blocking urlopen with a 4 second timeout runs inside an async request handler

evidence.observed: MEASURED by reading the call chain. fetch_store_version (line 81) is a plain `def` that calls urllib.request.urlopen with timeout=4, and it is called from `async def get_extension_version` (line 211). urllib is synchronous and the call is not offloaded, so the coroutine blocks the single event loop for up to four seconds on every cache miss - during which NO other request is served.

findings.impact: One slow or unresponsive Chrome Web Store endpoint stalls the entire API for up to 4 s per request, not just the version check. On a single-process uvicorn (which is what this box runs) that is a self-inflicted DoS whenever the store is slow, and it is reached from the extension's own update check.

fix.approach: Offload the blocking call to a thread. Keep fetch_store_version synchronous - it is correct as a function; only its CALL SITE is wrong.

# Blocking here is invisible to a correctness assertion, so measure concurrency.
import asyncio, time
from unittest.mock import patch


def test_version_check_does_not_block_the_event_loop(client):
    def slow_store_call():
        time.sleep(1.5)          # stands in for a slow store lookup
        return "9.9.9"

    async def concurrent_probe():
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        task = asyncio.create_task(asyncio.to_thread(
            lambda: client.get("/api/extension/version")))
        await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
        await asyncio.to_thread(
            lambda: client.get("/api/health"))   # must return WHILE the first is in flight
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - t0
        await task
        return elapsed

    with patch("server.routes_extension.fetch_store_version", slow_store_call):
        elapsed = asyncio.run(concurrent_probe())
    assert elapsed < 1.4, (
        f"health probe was delayed to {elapsed:.2f}s - the store call is blocking the loop")

findings.title: Screen vision LLM calls bypass metering entirely

findings.title: process_payment miscalculates token allocation by a factor of 10,000

findings.title: The permanent deletion GDPR endpoint is inert while the suite reports green

findings.title: Flat prices undervalue real token costs after the unit migration

evidence.observed: MEASURED: In server/draft.py:28, DRAFT_COST is 2.0 tokens ($0.0002 at 100 tokens/cent). In server/main.py:1848-1856, audio transcription debits max(1.0, math.ceil(duration/3600.0)) tokens — exactly 1 token ($0.0001) per hour of audio, against a real OpenRouter Gemini/Whisper upstream cost of ~$0.05 to $0.15 (500 to 1,500 tokens). findings.title: Chart theme variables omitted in light mode and undefined in chart context

findings.title: Duplicate and divergent primitive implementations in os.jsx vs the dedicated primitives

evidence.observed: MEASURED: EmptyState and Kbd are duplicated in os.jsx with legacy styling (os.jsx EmptyState uses legacy .panel and hardcoded text-white bg-[var(--accent)]), while EmptyState.jsx uses Stitch v6 Luminous Glass (bg-surface-container-lowest/70 backdrop-blur-xl border-outline-variant/20). findings.title: Radius and spacing token scale drift between CSS custom properties, Tailwind utilities and the specs

evidence.observed: MEASURED: index.css:156-158 defines --radius-sm: 0.75rem (12px), --radius-md: 1rem (16px), --radius-lg: 1.5rem (24px). web/DESIGN.md:43-45 documents --radius-sm: 8px, --radius-md: 12px, --radius-lg: 16px. Furthermore, @theme inline in index.css does not map --radius-* tokens into Tailwind v4 utilities.

findings.impact: Inconsistent corner radiuses across cards, buttons, and inputs: rounded-lg in Tailwind produces 8px while var(--radius-sm) produces 12px.

fix.approach: Harmonize radius scale to canonical Stitch v6 tokens (sm: 8px, md: 12px, lg: 16px, xl: 24px) and map into @theme inline in index.css.

findings.title: Monochromatic tertiary hue collision and surface elevation collapse in the design tokens

evidence.observed: MEASURED: In index.css, --st-primary is teal #78F5E5 (hue 172.3°) and --st-tertiary is aqua #9AEFEA (hue 176.5°) with a collision delta of only 4.2° (spec called for warm rose #FFB2BE, hue 350.6°, delta 178.3°). findings.impact: Loss of semantic visual hierarchy: tertiary highlights blend into primary controls, and surface cards lack visual elevation above the background canvas.

fix.approach: Restore warm rose tertiary accent (--st-tertiary: #FFB2BE) and give base surface a distinct elevation step (--st-surface: #14171A) over canvas #0E1113.

findings.title: Touch targets below the 44px minimum on interactive controls

evidence.observed: MEASURED: OfflineBanner reconnect button specifies min-h-[32px] (32px height) and PrivacyPolicyView CTA specifies min-h-[36px] (36px height), both failing the WCAG 2.1 AA / 2.5.5 accessible touch target floor of 44px.

findings.impact: Touch target accessibility violation: interactive buttons are difficult to tap accurately on mobile screens and touch devices.

fix.approach: Update interactive controls to min-h-[44px] (or min-w-[44px] min-h-[44px]) ensuring touch target accessibility compliance.

findings.title: Motion duration and easing inconsistent between token file, Tailwind utilities and index.css

evidence.observed: MEASURED: motion_tokens.json specifies durations fast: 120ms, medium: 180ms, standard: 240ms. index.css:116-119 specifies --motion-micro: 150ms, --motion-standard: 250ms, --motion-emphasis: 400ms. Tailwind utilities operate on default unmapped 150ms/200ms/300ms scales.

findings.impact: Inconsistent transition and animation cadences across interactive components and route transitions.

fix.approach: Unify motion tokens in index.css with motion_tokens.json and map duration/easing variables into @theme inline.

findings.title: ActivityView renders NotificationsView without onNavigate, stripping its action buttons

evidence.observed: MEASURED: ActivityView accepts no onNavigate prop (ActivityView({ admin, initialMode })) and mounts <NotificationsView /> at line 109 with no props. NotificationsView:262 only renders jump action buttons if onNavigate is truthy ({item.link && onNavigate && ...}), so all notification action buttons are stripped when viewed in ActivityView.

findings.impact: Users reviewing notifications in the Activity tab cannot jump to the linked coursework or study materials; buttons are invisible.

fix.approach: Pass onNavigate from App.jsx through ActivityView to <NotificationsView onNavigate={onNavigate} />.

findings.title: Five orphaned components (96+ KB) with zero incoming imports

evidence.claim_as_reported: The report lists five orphaned admin/dispatch components totalling 96+ KB.
evidence.why_not_verified: DUPLICATE of CONV-04, which was verified independently and MEASURED: all five named here plus AdminAgentChat have 0 inbound importers. findings.title: SettingsApp has no hashchange listener, so deep-linked subnav pills desynchronise

evidence.observed: MEASURED: SettingsApp:111 initializes activeSection state from window.location.hash once during mount. There is no window.addEventListener('hashchange', ...) effect in SettingsApp, so deep links or browser back/forward hash changes desynchronize the active subnav pill from the address bar.

findings.impact: Navigating between settings sections via URL hash or browser back/forward buttons fails to switch the visible settings section.

fix.approach: Add useEffect listening to 'hashchange' in SettingsApp.jsx to update activeSection when the hash changes.

findings.title: N+1 query: the study materials API fires a separate query per card state

evidence.observed: MEASURED: In get_study_decks (GET /api/study/decks), after fetching materials in one query, lines 88-105 iterate `for m in materials:` and execute `db.query(StudyCardState).filter(StudyCardState.user_id == user.id, StudyCardState.material_id == m.id).all()` individually for every material. 50 materials trigger 51 SQL queries.

findings.impact: Latency scales linearly with study material volume: fetching study decks creates avoidable SQLite query lock churn and delays rendering.

fix.approach: Batch fetch card states in a single query: `db.query(StudyCardState).filter(StudyCardState.user_id == user.id, StudyCardState.material_id.in_([m.id for m in materials])).all()` and group in-memory.

findings.title: Post-stream AI detection delays the done frame and can diverge from what the user saw

evidence.claim_as_reported: Raw chunks stream to the client, then detection and possible rewrite run; the user has already seen text that may not be what is stored, with a silent gap before done.
evidence.why_not_verified: DUPLICATE of TEST-06 (same defect reported from the latency and the testing angle). NOT VERIFIED - the stream path was not traced in this pass. The claim is coherent and matches the architecture AGENTS.md describes (ensure_human_standard runs after generation), so it is plausible; plausibility is not verification.

findings.promote_when: Resolve jointly with TEST-06: trace /api/agent/chat/stream after the final chunk, confirm whether a rewrite can change the persisted reply, and decide whether to emit a correction frame.

findings.title: The background monitor loop blocks the event loop for ~220ms every 60s and rewrites 3.2 MB when idle

evidence.observed: MEASURED: snapshot_once() takes 203.55ms wall time / 197.10ms CPU time and is executed synchronously directly inside `async def run_monitors_loop()` every 60 seconds without asyncio.to_thread(). It parses JSONL line-by-line, computes SHA256 hashes, runs 8 DB queries, and rewrites the entire history file on each tick.

findings.impact: Every 60 seconds, the main asyncio event loop freezes for ~200ms of synchronous CPU/disk work, delaying HTTP requests and health checks while writing 192 MB/hr to disk when idle.

fix.approach: Run snapshot_once() off the main asyncio event loop via asyncio.to_thread(), and gate _trim_history() so it only rewrites when lines exceed HISTORY_MAX_LINES + 200.

findings.title: The Telegram agent loop polls SQLite synchronously every 3.0s when no bots are connected

evidence.observed: MEASURED: telegram_agent_loop() executes _connected_users() every 3.0 seconds (POLL_INTERVAL=3.0) synchronously on the asyncio event loop. _connected_users() runs `db.query(User).filter(User.settings.is_not(None)).all()`, loading all users and parsing settings blobs every 3 seconds even when zero users have bot tokens.

findings.impact: Continuous idle SQLite read lock contention and CPU polling churn for a feature used by a fraction of accounts.

fix.approach: Cache connected bot token count or use an async/thread query with a longer idle interval (e.g. 30s when no bots connected, 3s when bots active).

findings.title: The replace-on-write rule for scoped settings lets concurrent tabs clobber each other

evidence.observed: MEASURED: REPLACE_ON_WRITE = frozenset({'scoped'}) replaces current['scoped'] with copy.deepcopy(v) rather than merging. Because the client in scopedSettings.js merges into an in-memory module cache in one tab, concurrent tabs saving overrides clobber each other's path overrides.

findings.impact: Users configuring overrides in multiple tabs or devices silently lose settings when the second write overwrites the full scoped dictionary.

fix.approach: Deep merge scoped setting paths on the server by path key (`current['scoped'][path] = v[path]`), or listen to storage/broadcast events on the client.

findings.title: Shape assertions in test_gdocs_exporter pass on uncorrected text

evidence.observed: MEASURED: test_originality_compliance_self_correct only asserts `isinstance(corrected_text, str)` and `len(corrected_text) > 0`. If self_correct_content returns the uncorrected input text unchanged, the test passes.

findings.impact: Vacuous test assertion: regressions in the self-correction humanization pipeline pass silently.

fix.approach: Assert that corrected_text differs from flagged_text and that metrics['burstiness'] improves or meets compliance thresholds.

findings.title: A deterministic mock fallback in harness.py bypasses the self-healing repair loop under test

evidence.observed: MEASURED: test_flash_pro_self_healing_loop passes required_keys=['status', 'model']. When DeepSeek API is unreachable in tests, _mock_fallback returns mock_data already containing 'status' and 'model'. Missing keys is empty, so line 187 returns on attempt 1 (healed=False) and the self-healing repair pass (lines 191-207) is never entered.

findings.impact: The self-healing JSON repair pipeline is completely unexercised in unit tests despite appearing tested.

fix.approach: Provide required keys not present in initial mock payload (e.g. required_keys=['status', 'model', 'synthesized_rubric_analysis']), forcing execution of the Flash repair loop.

findings.title: The persistent test DB with no teardown leaks state across tests and causes run-order flakes

evidence.observed: MEASURED: test_helpotron.db is a persistent file (currently 9.3 MB on disk). client fixture initializes tables with init_db() but performs no rollback or table truncation between test cases. State leaks across tests, causing run-order flakes.

findings.impact: Accumulated test database pollution forces tests to use uuid workarounds, breaks exact row count assertions, and causes order-dependent flakiness.

fix.approach: Implement per-test SQLite SAVEPOINT/rollback or table truncation in a pytest autouse fixture in conftest.py.

findings.title: AI detection runs after tokens have streamed, with zero test coverage

evidence.claim_as_reported: Detection and a possible rewrite happen after raw chunks have already reached the client, so the persisted reply can differ from what the user read - and no test covers the ordering.
evidence.why_not_verified: DUPLICATE of LAT-05 (latency angle). NOT VERIFIED - the stream path was not traced. The reported line range is specific, so this is cheap to confirm.

findings.promote_when: Resolve jointly with LAT-05. The test that should exist asserts ORDERING: that no persisted rewrite can occur without the client being told. A test asserting only that detection ran would pass against the bug.

findings.title: Third-party AI subprocessors are undisclosed in the privacy policy

findings.impact: Regulatory non-compliance under GDPR Article 28 / CCPA: third-party AI subprocessors handling user text are undisclosed in the privacy policy.

fix.approach: Add Sapling and Pangram to THIRD_PARTIES in PrivacyPolicyView.jsx and PRIVACY_POLICY.md disclosing their role in AI detector verification.

findings.title: No corporate entity is named in the Terms, threatening the arbitration and liability clauses

findings.impact: Legal unenforceability risk: limitation of liability and arbitration clauses require clear identification of the contracting corporate entity.

fix.approach: Formally define Helpotron Autonomous Systems LLC in the preamble of TermsOfServiceView.jsx and Section 1 of PRIVACY_POLICY.md as the contracting entity.

findings.title: Obsolete auth and data-handling claims in the Terms and Privacy Policy

findings.title: Referral rewards are described in a way the wallet does not deliver

findings.title: COPPA age limit and data retention are inconsistent between the Terms, the cookie banner and the deletion code

decisions.subject: Tier allowances and the margin model
decisions.ruling: Tier allowances stay as they are: basic 30,000 / pro 100,000 / elite 270,000, trial 15,000, testing 10,000. The owner's intent is a mathematically ensured profit margin per tier, because the token unit is 1/100 of a cent.
decisions.consequence: The BALANCE IS THE CEILING. Never add a plan-based charge exemption. A negative balance is honest and self-blocks the account until a top-up; that is the design, not a bug.
decisions.standing_hazard: plan == 'elite' bypasses are a RECURRING class in this codebase - removed at least twice and found alive again in routes_dump.py. It is why ECON-04 is listed as a sweep, not a one-line fix.

decisions.subject: Refunding is earn-only
decisions.ruling: Tokens are consumed, not refunded. Nothing is charged before the work runs, so a task that fails outright is simply never charged - there is nothing to refund.
decisions.consequence: The pre-flight gate checks eligibility only (has_usage_balance) and takes no money. Settlement charges the measured cost after the fact (ledger_watermark -> usage_cents_since -> charge_actual_usage). The old up-front charge plus refund branch was deleted because with nothing charged, a refund would MINT a free token.
decisions.consequence_of_removing_it: Test TASK-02's assertions were rewritten to the new semantics: a session that failed outright, or disconnected before doing real work and collected nothing, is simply never charged; a session that ran steps and then disconnected still pays for what it used.

durable_notes.lesson: with_for_update() IS A NO-OP ON SQLITE
durable_notes.detail: Verified by compiling the statement: the emitted SQL contains no FOR UPDATE. Any fix whose whole approach is 'add with_for_update()' is INERT on this database - it will pass review, pass tests, and change nothing. Two mechanisms actually work: BEGIN IMMEDIATE (serialises a read-modify-write) and json_set/json_extract in a single statement (atomic with no lock).
durable_notes.why_it_matters: REL-01 is money. The obvious fix was the wrong one.

durable_notes.lesson: A read-then-write on the JSON settings blob cannot be fixed by locking advice - the change must go INSIDE the statement
durable_notes.detail: Measured: two concurrent 400-token debits against a balance of 1000 left 600 before the fix (one debit swallowed) and 200 after (credits.debit_tokens_atomic).
durable_notes.why_it_matters: The same shape recurs wherever settings.token_balance is read, modified and written.

durable_notes.lesson: A test double that ignores the write proves nothing
durable_notes.detail: The first merge test passed straight through the REL-02 bug because its fake DB never applied db.execute(...). The double must capture AND apply the statement.
durable_notes.why_it_matters: This is how a green suite coexists with a live defect - TEST-01, TEST-02 and TEST-07 are the same family.

durable_notes.lesson: The test DB is a persistent FILE
durable_notes.detail: conftest points at sqlite:///./test_helpotron.db with no per-test rollback, so an assertion on an exact global row count breaks in a full-suite run because the previous run's rows are still there. Use a unique public_id / idempotency key per run.
durable_notes.why_it_matters: Three v1 tests failed only in full-suite runs for exactly this reason. TEST-05 is the durable fix; the uuid workaround is a symptom.

durable_notes.detail: is_unmetered() is operator-only by construction (security.is_admin_user); its docstring records that the elite short-circuit was removed once and survived anyway.
durable_notes.why_it_matters: A paid tier consuming unbounded upstream spend was live in routes_dump.py until v1.

durable_notes.lesson: create_all() does NOT add an index to a table that already exists
durable_notes.detail: Model-declared index=True only helps a fresh DB. Measured now: 70 index=True declarations against exactly 1 CREATE INDEX statement, so the live DB carries almost none of them.
durable_notes.why_it_matters: REL-05, and it is why every new UNIQUE constraint (REL-03) needs an explicit idempotent CREATE INDEX in the migration block.

durable_notes.lesson: A feature can be 100% implemented and 100% dead
durable_notes.detail: The avatar endpoint existed with no caller. CONV-02 is the same class: seven study-material export endpoints with zero frontend callers.
durable_notes.why_it_matters: Grep for a CALLER, not just for the code. A passing test over an endpoint proves the endpoint works, not that anyone can reach it.

durable_notes.detail: Tokens = usage, in settings.token_balance (a JSON blob, not a column). Credits = earned-only discounts, in users.discount_balance + discount_spillover, created solely by earn_credits, applied as a percent discount on an order.
durable_notes.why_it_matters: UI-05 is exactly this confusion in the UI - the CREDITS label renders token_balance.

durable_notes.lesson: The server is the only config that counts - server/.env is a decoy
durable_notes.detail: Nothing reads server/.env. server/config.py:15 sets env_file to the REPO ROOT, and server/llm.py:18 load_dotenv()s the same root file with override=True. A key put in server/.env is present-but-inert, which is indistinguishable from working until you read it back through the app.
durable_notes.why_it_matters: A rotation was performed into server/.env and had no effect. Also why TURNSTILE_* looked configurable while the gate was off.

durable_notes.lesson: Duplicate auth logic is how a new credential type gets forgotten
durable_notes.detail: Two live instances were found: routes_features.get_current_authenticated_user had its own copy of the cookie/JWT/session logic and never learned about API keys; routes_organization had its own cookie-only get_current_user. Both now delegate to the shared resolver.
durable_notes.why_it_matters: Before declaring a credential done, grep for EVERY place that parses Authorization.

durable_notes.lesson: Never restart a live service as your verification
durable_notes.detail: Order is edit -> ast.parse/import check -> suite -> restart -> verify the endpoint. The suite imports server.main, so it catches a SyntaxError in a second. A restart against a broken file turns a syntax error into an outage, and Restart=always then hides it as 'activating' while it crash-loops (81 restarts, presented as a login failure).
durable_notes.why_it_matters: This took the production site down once already.

durable_notes.lesson: A test that bypasses the link that is broken will pass forever
durable_notes.detail: Round 1 of the scroll fix drove executeReturnedActions directly and stubbed the server; the real path is model -> fenced block -> server validation -> control_actions -> executor. The harness proved nothing about delivery.
durable_notes.why_it_matters: When a feature spans client and server, the repro must go through BOTH.

execution_order.theme: Stop the data loss and the blank screens
execution_order.rationale: Two of these silently destroy user data or money; two make the product unusable for a signed-in user. Fix them before anything cosmetic.

execution_order.theme: Stop the product lying to the user
execution_order.rationale: CONV-01 hands a user a fabricated BIO-309 assignment and reports success; LEG-01 is the highest-consequence finding in the audit; UI-05 mislabels a balance. TEST-08 and UI-09 are one-liners that ride along.

execution_order.theme: Unblock work that is already built
execution_order.rationale: Highest value per hour in the whole plan: the export suite, the triage workflow and the orphan cleanup are already implemented or already dead. This is wiring and deletion.

Five independent blocking calls in async handlers, all on the API's hot paths, all one-line fixes once located. They are grouped because they share one test shape (a concurrency probe) and one reviewer.
This box has frozen twice. These four determine whether it happens a third time. EFF-07 is the guard that does not guard; EFF-02 is 2.16 GiB idle.

DSGN-01 and DSGN-04 are verified and user-visible (an unreadable label; a third-party request from a self-hosted app). The rest are drift and should be swept in one pass with DSGN-01's contrast work rather than four separate ones.

ECON-04's report claimed ~12 bypass sites and only 2 were verified and fixed. Sweep the rest, then settle ECON-05 (are the surviving flat prices floors or the whole charge) and REL-05's index migration.

TEST-05 is the leverage: a per-test rollback removes the uuid workaround from every test that carries it AND removes a class of run-order flakes. The others are tests that cannot fail for the reason they name - and they are only provable once the DB is isolated.

execution_order.theme: Compliance copy and the open unknowns
execution_order.rationale: Copy goes last because it must describe the product AFTER the fixes land, not before. The three SEC open items are unknown, not clean - SEC-OPEN-A (IDOR) is the largest single unknown in the audit and should be run early if capacity allows, but it is placed here because it is a sweep rather than a fix.

open_questions.recommendation: Yes, with a 15-minute idle window. The RAM is the scarcer resource on this box, and hip_humanizer already degrades to the documented fallback path when the endpoint is unreachable.

open_questions.recommendation: Floors. The finding must then be narrowed to naming which floors no longer bind.

open_questions.recommendation: Owner decision. Inventing an entity name into a legal document would be worse than the gap - do not edit legal copy unilaterally.

open_questions.recommendation: Per-material, next to the material they export. A batch control invites a download of everything, which is a different feature.
